title_original: This Black Friday, Shop From Artists and Art Nonprofits
excerpt_original: Small presses, artists’ editions, and Native American trading posts are just some of the places we recommend you shop from this holiday season.

blocks.text: From high-end brands shaving deceptively large sums off their already price-hiked catalogs to the ye olde tradition of department stores luring families in with a handsome deal, Black Friday is every American corporation’s wet dream. Here at Hyperallergic , we encourage you to dig a little deeper into your purses this year for the independent retailers, artists, and nonprofits out there. You (and your loved ones) will be pleasantly surprised by the gems you find on our list of small businesses, imprints, print shops, and Native American trading posts to keep on your radar this holiday season.

blocks.caption: Beaded wallet for sale on Blackfish Trading Post's webstore (image courtesy Blackfish Trading Post)

blocks.text: “Art has been a part of my culture since time immemorial, and I am honored to continue that tradition today,” Denise Gloria (Elwha Klallam) writes in her biography page on the Blackfish Trading Post website. That sentiment extends to the 18 other artists spotlighted on the online store, including beaders, textile artists, painters, and jewelers. Operated by the Lower Elwha Klallam Tribal Vocational Rehabilitation Program in Port Angeles, Washington, the trading post helps Native Americans with disabilities obtain career exposure and experience while preserving cultural heritage.
